name_note: GTDB splits the classical genus Phascolarctobacterium into several genera, of which Phascolarctobacterium_A is one; the genomes placed here carry the NCBI genus name Phascolarctobacterium.

sentences.text: Phascolarctobacterium can produce short-chain fatty acids, including acetate and propionate.
Phascolarctobacterium succinatutens, isolated from the feces of healthy human adults, used only succinate and did not ferment other short-chain fatty acids or carbohydrates tested.
When cocultured with a xylan-utilizing, succinate-producing gut bacterium, succinate became undetectable and propionate was formed.
